case_name: Sri Bapi Acharjee vs The State Of Tripura

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sri Bapi Acharjee, Sri Satya Ranjan Acharjee, Smt. Anita Acharjee, Sri Nanda Lal Acharjee
parties.respondent_defendant: The State of Tripura, Smt. Supriya Acharjee

facts_of_case: Petitioners filed for quashing of FIR dated 28.08.2020 and subsequent orders passed in the case.

legal_principles.principle: Criminal law should not be used as a tool for harassment or vendetta.
legal_principles.held: The allegations in a criminal complaint must be scrutinized with care to ensure that they disclose a prima facie case before subjecting individuals to the rigors of a criminal trial.
cited_cases: P.V. Krishnabhat & Anr. v. The State of Karnataka & Ors., (2025) SCC OnLine SC 484

legal_principles.principle: Continuation of criminal proceedings in the absence of a prima facie case would amount to an abuse of the process of law and result in a miscarriage of justice.
legal_principles.held: The continuation of criminal proceedings in such circumstances would amount to an abuse of the process of law and result in a miscarriage of justice.
cited_cases: P.V. Krishnabhat & Anr. v. The State of Karnataka & Ors., (2025) SCC OnLine SC 484

legal_principles.principle: A criminal trial leading to an eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scars upon the accused, and such an exercise must be discouraged.
legal_principles.held: It has been highlighted by this Court in varied instances, that a criminal trial leading to an eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scars upon the accused, and such an exercise must, therefore, be discouraged.
cited_cases: Kahkashan Kausar @Sonam & Ors. v. State of Bihar & Ors., (2022) 6 SCC 599

outcome.final_order: The petition was allowed, and the FIR and subsequent orders were quashed.
